title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is in a state of flux, with SpaceX grappling with both operational challenges and a burgeoning satellite launch schedule. Meanwhile, geopolitical maneuvers like Serbia's signing of the Artemis Accords signal a shifting landscape in international space collaboration.

themes.title: SpaceX's Launch Conundrum
themes.body: Despite its impressive track record, SpaceX faces hurdles in scaling operations, particularly with the aborted Starship Flight 13. The company's ability to juggle multiple satellite launches while addressing these setbacks will be closely watched.

themes.title: Geopolitical Space Agreements
themes.body: Serbia's recent signing of the Artemis Accords highlights a growing trend of nations aligning with U.S. space initiatives. This move may bolster Serbia's defense capabilities while deepening its ties to Western space endeavors.

themes.title: Funding for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup, which adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflects a heightened focus on safeguarding U.S. interests in orbit. This financial commitment underscores the increasing recognition of space as a strategic domain.

themes.title: Emerging Defense Technologies
themes.body: As companies like Anduril and L3Harris collaborate on tactical satellite constellations, the defense sector is clearly pivoting towards advanced technologies for space operations. The intersection of AI and defense is also gaining traction, as evidenced by the surge in 'AI for Defense' startups.
